note: Hand-edited source for the Atlas (Meitou only; the squad record window's Atlas tab, Atlas.cs). gen_atlas.py turns it into x_atlas.json, adding the named outlaws and every gossip line the helper listens for. Our own words, after the Kenshi wiki and kenshimap; ASCII only. places: TOWN record names (base records). known: common knowledge once the place is on your map. explored: what you learn by going there. people: CHARACTER record names. hidden: nobody says where they are; they appear blurred (vague) after one rumour, placed after two, fully once met. rumours: dialogue id prefixes of gossip about them (bosses_*.json, x_rumours.json and so on). wanted_for: what the posters say.

Blister Hill.known: The Holy Nation's capital. The Holy Lord Phoenix sits on his throne there.
explored: Two towns in one: the Phoenix's walled quarter, and everyone else outside it.
Paladins at every corner. Pray loudly, and do not be a Shek.

Bad Teeth.known: A Holy Nation town that guards the pass into the green valleys.
explored: Farmers, priests and a lot of Holy Sentinels with nothing to do.
What comes down the pass from the wilds gets stopped here, or eaten.

Stack.known: A Holy Nation town between the Hub and the Western Hive. Traders like it; so do thieves.
explored: Good shops for a frontier town.
The Nation watches the road to the Hub from here, and the Hive watches back.

Rebirth.known: Where the Holy Nation sends sinners to work until Okran forgives them. He rarely does.
explored: A mine with walls, and slaves who were citizens last week.
Nobody leaves Rebirth by asking.

Okran's Fist.known: A Holy Nation fortress on the north-east road.
explored: Paladins and Sentinels, drilled and bored.
The Nation's door to the north-east. Closed to most.

Okran's Shield.known: A Holy Nation fortress that closes the valley road like a gate.
explored: Built across a choke-point; every caravan passes under its walls.
The garrison stops the Skin Bandits coming down from the dark.

Heft.known: Capital of the United Cities. Emperor Tengu holds court there.
explored: Nobles, samurai and the Emperor's palace. Money talks; everyone else bows.
Lord Ohta keeps his house here too, and the Emperor's ear.

Stoat.known: The last United Cities town before the eastern desert. Lord Inaba governs it.
explored: Fed by the stone camp and the slave farm nearby.
A good place to buy water and a bad place to be a runaway slave.

Sho-Battai.known: A big United Cities town in the middle of the desert. Lord Nagata rules it.
explored: The only hat shop in the Cities, and a thieves' guild nobody admits to.
It eats what Port North digs up.

Brink.known: A United Cities town on the coast. Lady Tsugi governs it.
explored: It lives on what Eyesocket's slaves produce.
Reavers walk the roads outside like they own them. Some days they do.

Bark.known: A United Cities town built around old lagoons on the north-east coast. Lady Sanda governs it.
explored: Half a port, with no ships. Supplies come from Port North and Port South.
Fishing smells and noble perfume, both strong.

Drifter's Last.known: A United Cities town in the south-west, ringed by farms. Lady Merin lives there.
explored: Farms outside, guards inside, and trouble from the hills now and then.
Plenty of newcomers start out here with nothing.

Catun.known: A United Cities fortress town on a plateau in the Bonefields.
explored: Home of the Catun Scrapmasters, the best robotics workshop in the Cities.
Well walled. The Bonefields are no place to be caught outside.

Heng.known: The Empire's trading town, joined to Trader's Edge by a metal bridge.
explored: Everything has a price here, and a Guild man to take a cut of it.
The bridge to Trader's Edge is worth the walk.

Trader's Edge.known: The Traders Guild's own settlement, on a plateau next to Heng.
explored: Where the Guild keeps its ledgers and its friends.
Samurai guard it. The Guild pays them well.

Mourn.known: A mining town built inside an old metal ruin. A slave revolt broke it.
explored: The Tech Hunters own it now, and the Cities still say it is theirs.
Empty mines and angry ghosts, as the locals tell it.

Admag.known: Capital of the Shek Kingdom, on a hill with one way in. Esata the Stone Golem rules there.
explored: The Hundred Guardians stand at the gate. They are not a ceremony.
Honour matters here more than cats. Fight well or do not fight.

Squin.known: A Shek town east of Admag, run on wind power.
explored: The lights flicker when the wind drops. Nobody here complains about it.
A Shek town, but traders of every kind pass through.

Last Stand.known: A Shek fortress where old warriors go to die well, fighting the Bugmaster's spiders.
explored: Grey warriors sharpening blades they will not bring back.
Arach is just over the hill. You can hear it at night.

The Great Fortress.known: A Shek fortress, mostly ruined, near New Kralia.
explored: Only the police station and the hall still stand.
Grand name, broken walls.

The Hub.known: A broken town between the Shek and the Holy Nation, fought over for years.
explored: The Trade Ninjas run it now, quietly.
Cheap beds, cheap bar, and nobody asks where you got it.

Shark.known: The Swamp's big town, full of ex-slaves, gangs and worse. The Swampers say they run it.
explored: The Hounds actually run it. Everybody knows; nobody says.
You can buy anything in Shark. You can also be bought.

Mud Town.known: A Swamper village north of Shark.
explored: Stilts, mud and people who would rather not be found.
Odd folk drift in here, some worth hiring.

Rot.known: A Hounds village in the Swamp.
explored: Ears and Big Grim's people. Friendly, if you are one of them.
There is not much in Rot but the Hounds and the smell.

World's End.known: A Tech Hunter town on a mountain, inside Holy Nation lands.
explored: The Machinists build things the Nation would burn.
It stays free by being useful, and by being hard to climb.

Black Scratch.known: The Tech Hunters' home, built around an ancient structure on a hill.
explored: The Great Library is here. Bring cats, and an interest in old things.
The Tech Hunter bar has stories. Most are true.

Flats Lagoon.known: A Tech Hunter town by the lagoon. Safer than it looks.
explored: Harpooners on the shore, Hive caravans on the road. They do not always agree.
A good place to rest between bad places.

Spring.known: The Anti-Slavers' mountain base. Tinfist is there.
explored: Built to be defended, and it has been.
Every slave who reaches Spring is free. Every slaver who reaches it is not.

Black Desert City.known: A town of skeletons, from after the Second Empire. No humans live there.
explored: Repair beds instead of beds. The bar sells things no person needs.
Sadneil keeps the Skeleton Bar. He remembers a long time.
Red cloaks, sharp blades and long memories.
They pay for cannibal heads. They ask fewer questions about the rest.

Mongrel.known: A walled town in the fog. Nobody goes out at night there.
explored: The Fogmen come to the gates most nights.
The people here are hard, because the soft ones were taken.

Western Hive.known: The Western Hive's village, on an island in acid water.
explored: The water burns. The drones do not mind.
Soldier drones meet you at the shore. Be polite.

Cannibal Capital.known: Once a town called Deadcat. The cannibals took it.
explored: It looks like a town from a distance. That is the trap.
The Gran' Wizard lives here, among more cannibals than you can count.

First Village.known: A cannibal village in the north of Darkfinger.
explored: The Meat Lord's table is here, and the cages that feed it.
Do not accept an invitation to dinner.

Cannibals.known: A cannibal village on the plains.
explored: Alder Quill's kitchen and Mother Brine's cure-house, if the stories are true. They are.
The smoke comes from the cure-house. Do not think about it.

Throne of the Bugmaster.known: A crater full of spiders in Arach.
explored: Skin spiders and blood spiders, more than anyone has counted.
Something sits on a throne at the bottom. The spiders guard it.

Cat-Lon's Exile.known: Domes deep in the Ashlands, under something huge hanging in the sky.
explored: The Second Empire's exiles live here, and their Stormthralls.
One of the old empire's own, still alive, still angry.

Tower of Fog.known: A lone tower on an island. Fogmen live there.
explored: Fogmen everywhere, and one of their princes.
Nobody goes in by choice.

Skinhouse HQ.known: Where the Skin Bandits live, somewhere in the dark lands.
explored: Peeler machines. People go in whole.
Savant rules it from a throne.

Swamp Ninja Base.known: A hidden base of the Swamp Ninjas.
explored: Ninjas of every rank, and Shade over them.
Hidden well; that was the point.

Cactus Den.known: A watchtower in Spine Canyon, home of the Sand Ninjas.
explored: Sand Ninja Oni lives at the top. Walking in uninvited makes enemies.
Close to Tengu's Vault, and they like it that way.

Red Sabre Hideout.known: The Red Sabres' hideout in the south-west Swamp.
explored: Twenty-odd Red Sabres and their boss.
Good gear inside, for whoever survives taking it.

Dust King Tower.known: A fortified tower in the Border Zone. The Dust King's.
explored: Walls, a gate and crossbows on the walls. Dust Bandits by the dozen.
The Dust King does not come down.

Fort Simion.known: The Rebel Farmers' fort in Sinkuun.
explored: Swamp domes and shacks, and Boss Simion over them.
Farmers who stopped paying the Holy Nation, and lived.

Cult Village.known: A village on the coast where the Preacher's cult lives.
explored: They say blood in the soil brings a harvest. They test it.
Do not get caught here.

Tower of Abuse.known: An old lab in Venge. The Thrall Masters use it.
explored: Prisoners on the top floor. Agnu, among them, if the stories are right.
Venge's lasers make the walk there worse.

Tengu's Vault.known: The United Cities' prison in the Skimsands.
explored: Samurai guards, a Warden, floors of cells.
Those inside were put there for good.

Flotsam Village.known: Where the Flotsam Ninjas hide, somewhere in the Hidden Forest.
explored: Refugees and deserters from the Holy Nation, still praying to Okran in their own way.
Moll leads them. The Nation wants her head.

Port North.known: A slavers' work camp in the Great Desert. Not a port at all.
explored: Stone and iron, dug by slaves.
Half the Cities eat because of this place.

Eyesocket.known: A slave camp on a hill by the coast.
explored: Slave Master Grande runs it.
Brink lives on what is dug here.

Slave Markets.known: Where slavers sell what they catch.
explored: Cages, buyers and a Slave Market Master.
Keep your papers close.

Black Dog HQ.known: The Black Dogs' snailhouse, west of Black Scratch.
explored: Thick walls, a good gate and short tempers.
Start nothing here.

Bast.known: A United Cities city the Holy Nation destroyed.
explored: Ruins and squatters now.
The war passed through and took everything.

Rebel Base.known: A small bar in the Border Zone where outlaws drink.
explored: The Trade Ninjas sell things there you cannot buy elsewhere.
Crossbows, blueprints, and no questions.
Manhunters, and nothing but.
They hunt people for money. You are people.

Clownsteady.known: A small United Cities town in the Hook, fed by the slave farms nearby.
explored: Compact, busy, and well supplied.
Ask the traders here; they carry things the bigger towns do not.

Port South.known: A slavers' stone camp in the desert. Like Port North, it is no port.
explored: Stone mines and ore, worked by slaves.
Slave Master Wada keeps the place running.

Stone Camp.known: A slavers' work camp between Stoat and Sho-Battai.
explored: Stone mines, and slaves who will die in them.
Slave Master Haga lives here, behind guards.

Slave Farm.known: A slavers' cactus farm near Heng.
explored: Rows of cactus as far as you can see, and the slaves who tend them.
Slave Mistress Ren rules it from a noble house.

Holy Mines.known: The Holy Nation's mines, worked by servants and prisoners.
explored: High Overseers with whips, and sinners with picks.
Five of them, scattered through the Nation's hills.

Holy Farm.known: Holy Nation farms on the green lands.
explored: Greenfruit, cotton, wheat. The Nation eats because of them.
Lower servants work; paladins watch.

Holy Military Base.known: Holy Nation outposts facing the Fog Islands.
explored: Built to hold back the Fogmen.
The soldiers here do not sleep well.

Waystation.known: Tech Hunter waystations on the long roads.
explored: A bed, a bar and a shop where there would otherwise be nothing.
Tech Hunters stop here on the way to the ruins.

Ark.known: The Reavers' stronghold, in Stobe's Garden.
explored: Cages for prisoners, and Reavers who think they are free men.
Valamon leads them from here.

Grayflayer Village.known: A Swamp village run by the Grayflayers.
explored: Big Gray's people. The Swampers' hardest gang.
Come with friends or do not come.

Iron HQ.known: The Skeleton Bandits' hold in the Crags.
explored: Metal walls, and old skeletons who decided to be bandits.
Elder leads them.

The Old Prison.known: A bandit stronghold south of Mourn.
explored: An old tower like a lab, and Gorrillo's bandits all over it.
Gorrillo himself is worth a fortune to someone.
They sell crabs. They also are crabs, in spirit.
The Crab Queen holds court here.

New Kralia.known: The hold of Kral's Chosen, south of Admag.
explored: Shek who think the Kingdom has gone soft. They fight anyone who comes.
Fifteen or twenty of them, all looking for a death worth singing about.

Shek Ruins.known: Broken buildings on a hill east of Admag.
explored: An old border post, wrecked in some war.
Nothing lives here but scavengers.

Southern Hive Village.known: A village of the Southern Hive.
explored: Pink-skinned hivers, nothing like the western kind.
They do not trade. They take.
Drones at work, soldiers at the edge, a trader if you are welcome.
Beak things and gorillos come at it often.

Distant Hive Village.known: A Western Hive village far from the others, in Sinkuun.
explored: Hivers far from home.
Quiet, until something comes out of the desert.

Settled Nomad Village.known: A Nomad village that stopped wandering, south of Raptor Island.
explored: They sell animals and packs.
Settled, but they still talk like the road is home.

Ashland Dome I.known: A great dome in the Ashlands, south-east of the Skinhouse.
explored: Many floors around a winding stair.
The Head of Agriculture is here, with thralls of the old Legion.

Deadhive Overrun.known: A dead town near the Fog Islands. The Fogmen have it.
explored: It was someone's town once.
The Fogmen took it, and they keep what they take.

Expedition 4.known: A town the Tech Hunters built and left, in Stobe's Garden.
explored: The wind generator still turns. Nobody knows why they left.
Their notes mention it.

Burn's Tower.known: A tower in the northern Floodlands, full of machines.
explored: Old technology everywhere.
A skeleton called Burn lives here, and he is not friendly yet.

Spider Factory.known: An old factory on the Forbidden Isle.
explored: Security spiders by the hundred.
Whatever it built, it is still building.

Holy Lord Phoenix.about: The Holy Nation's ruler, Okran's voice on earth. Each Phoenix follows the last; the faithful say it is the same man reborn.
Holy Lord Phoenix.wanted_for: Shek and Flotsam alike would pay for his end.

Emperor Tengu.about: Rules the Cities from his palace in Heft. Rich, old and suspicious.

Esata the Stone Golem.about: The Shek Queen. A warrior first, and a queen because of it.

Seto.about: The Queen's daughter. Some Shek hope she will change the Kingdom. Some fear she will.

Tinfist.about: A man in a machine body who wants every slave freed and every slaver dead.
Tinfist.wanted_for: The United Cities want him for war on their slave trade.

Moll.about: Leads the Flotsam Ninjas against the Holy Nation, from somewhere in the Hidden Forest.
Moll.wanted_for: The Holy Nation wants her for rebellion.

High Inquisitor Valtena.about: The Holy Nation's chief inquisitor. Sinners fear her; so do the faithful.

Lord Ohta.about: One of the Cities' great lords, never far from the Emperor.

Lord Nagata.about: Governs Sho-Battai and lives well on Port North's stone.

Lady Tsugi.about: Governs Brink. The Reavers on her roads are her problem, and she does not like problems.

Lord Inaba.about: Governs Stoat, the last town before the eastern desert.

Lord Yoshinaga.about: A lord of the Noble Circle, with a house and guards to match.

Longen.about: A Guild man with an Emperor's manners and a merchant's heart.

Cannibal Grand Wizard.about: Leader of all the cannibals. They say he hears a bell no one rings.
Cannibal Grand Wizard.wanted_for: Wanted everywhere for leading the cannibals.

Meat Lord.epithet: the host of the First Village
Meat Lord.about: A cannibal leader with manners, a long table and a full larder.
Meat Lord.wanted_for: Wanted for the people at his table.

Alder Quill.about: A Holy Nation kitchen priest who went over to the cannibals. Gentle, they say. That makes it worse.
Alder Quill.wanted_for: The Holy Nation and the Cities want him for what he cooks.

Mother Brine.about: Keeps the cannibals' cure-house. She fed them through the bad winter, and they never asked with what.
Mother Brine.wanted_for: The Holy Nation and the Cities want her for the cure-house.

Bugmaster.vague: A man who keeps spiders, somewhere in the east. Old Shek go to die fighting his pets.
Bugmaster.about: Sits on a throne at the bottom of a crater, guarded by more spiders than anyone has counted.
Bugmaster.wanted_for: A criminal of the old kind, wanted by every faction that has lost people to his spiders.

Mad Cat-Lon.vague: An exile of the old empire, still alive somewhere in the ash. Nobody who says so has been there.
Mad Cat-Lon.about: One of the Second Empire's own, living among his Stormthralls in the Ashlands. Old, and still angry.

Fog Prince.vague: The Fogmen have princes. One lives in a tower in the sea, they say.
Fog Prince.about: A prince of the Fogmen, in a tower full of them.

Savant.vague: The Skin Bandits have a master. He lives in the dark, and he collects skins.
Savant.about: Rules the Skin Bandits from his throne. The peelers are his.
Savant.wanted_for: Wanted for the people he has skinned.

Shade.vague: The Swamp Ninjas have a leader called Shade. Their base is somewhere in the wetlands.
Shade.about: Leads the Swamp Ninjas from their hidden base.
Shade.wanted_for: Wanted for the Swamp Ninjas' raids.

Sand Ninja Oni.vague: The Sand Ninjas answer to one called Oni. Somewhere in the canyons.
Sand Ninja Oni.about: Leads the Sand Ninjas from the top of a watchtower.

Red Sabre Boss.vague: The Red Sabres have a boss and a hideout, somewhere in the Swamp.
Red Sabre Boss.about: Runs the Red Sabres from their hideout.
Red Sabre Boss.wanted_for: Wanted for the Red Sabres' killings.

Dust King.about: King of the Dust Bandits, in a tower he never leaves.
Dust King.wanted_for: Wanted for leading the Dust Bandits.

Boss Simion.about: Leads farmers who stopped paying the Holy Nation, and lived.
Boss Simion.wanted_for: The Holy Nation wants him for rebellion.

The Preacher.about: Leads the coast cult. Blood in the soil, he preaches.

Valamon.vague: The Reavers have a leader, a Shek called Valamon. Their stronghold is somewhere in the far north.
Valamon.about: A Shek who left the Kingdom and leads the Reavers. Tall, fond of a fight, and not fond of anyone.
Valamon.wanted_for: Wanted for the Reavers' raids and slaving.

Sadneil.about: A skeleton who keeps the bar in Black Desert City and remembers the Second Empire.

Agnu.epithet: a prisoner of the Thrall Masters
Agnu.vague: Someone is held at the top of a tower in Venge, they say.
Agnu.about: Held by the Thrall Masters in the Tower of Abuse.

Gutterhead.about: Leads the Scavengers. Whatever you dropped, he has it.

Flying Bull.vague: A Shek called Flying Bull wants a war. Where he is, nobody says.
Flying Bull.about: A Shek warmonger who wants the old wars back.

Ghost.vague: A Shek they call Ghost. Seen once, never twice.
Ghost.about: A Shek outcast with a bounty and no fear.

Blue Eyes.epithet: an outlaw of the Holy Nation's borders
Blue Eyes.about: Wanted by the Holy Nation for heresy. Says what the priests will not.

Tora The Fearless.about: A Shek warrior the Kingdom calls dishonoured.

Slave Master Haga.about: Runs the Stone Camp and lives like a noble, behind noble guards.

Elder.about: An old skeleton who leads the Skeleton Bandits from the Crags.

Big Gray.about: Runs the Grayflayers, the Swamp's hardest gang.

Gorrillo.about: Leads the bandits holed up in the old prison south of Mourn.

Crab Queen.about: Leads the Crab Raiders from Crab Town.
Crab Queen.wanted_for: Wanted for the Crab Raiders' raids.

Slave Mistress Ren.about: Rules the cactus slave farm near Heng from a noble house.

Slave Master Wada.about: Keeps the slaves of Port South digging.

Big Grim.about: Leads the Hounds, who run Shark whatever the Swampers say.

Head of Agriculture.epithet: an old official of the Empire
Head of Agriculture.vague: Someone from the old empire still keeps a dome in the Ashlands, they say.
Head of Agriculture.about: An official of the old empire, still in his dome in the Ashlands with his thralls.
